description: Start a validation session for the user's integration. quickrun and run_workflow execute OUR curated workflow against a twin — green there says the provider behaves as documented, and says nothing about whether their integration wired to it correctly. This instead hands back a FRESH twin per provider and asks the user to point their app at it, then reads external provider traffic. Direct agent calls also appear there; caller identity is not established. Use it when someone wants their integration verified before launch, or when you have just run a happy path and need to say what it did and did not prove. Call once with `providers` to start, then again with the returned `session_id` after their app has run a flow. The matrix is returned before any traffic: pass `arm` with a probe ID before exercising the app. Send the returned request_headers on every provider request in that attempt, then pass `probe` and `run_id` to evaluate. Use `cancel: true` with `run_id` to abort or retry failed cleanup. Request logs alone do not prove application state or production readiness. For a supported payment-to-receipt integration, follow the returned receipt_delivery_v1 next action on the SAME session. Pass suite plus receipt_config with the app's exact webhook URL, test recipients and observable purchase marker. FetchSandbox freezes all four receipt rules for both same-customer and different-customer purchases. Configure the actual app with the issued twins, signing secret and request headers; then call execute:true with its run_id. FetchSandbox drives signed events and independently observes accepted email records. Keep every check and the observation windows in your report. If you cannot configure the app, report that blocker; reference tests cannot replace app execution. A verified receipt suite covers only its declared rules and windows, never all production behavior. This application suite requires sign-in.

app_base_url.description: Where their app is deployed, if known. Recorded so a later step can deliver webhooks to it.

arm.description: Probe ID from the matrix to arm before running the app. Requires session_id.

cancel.description: Abort the attempt or retry failed cleanup. Requires session_id and run_id; cannot combine with arm or probe.

execute.description: Drive the configured app and evaluate the frozen receipt suite. Requires session_id/run_id; configuration acknowledgment alone is not proof.

probe.description: Probe ID from the matrix to evaluate after running the app. Requires session_id and run_id.

providers.description: Provider slugs the app integrates, e.g. ['stripe'] or ['paddle','resend']. Required to start a session.

app_version.description: Declared application build identifier; not code attestation.

observation_seconds.description: Observation window after each checkpoint; default 2 seconds. Verdict covers only measured windows.

purchase_context.description: Application routing custom_data, e.g. test workspace ID. Never credentials.

purchase_marker.description: Where the normal receipt includes its Paddle transaction ID; same-record recipient/marker matching is required.

recipient_a.description: Expected test recipient for purchase A, fixed before execution.

recipient_b.description: Different test recipient for the different-customer case.

source_lookup_required.description: Whether the app reads the source provider during its normal webhook handler.

webhook_url.description: Exact normal application webhook URL, including path.

run_id.description: Attempt ID returned by arm. Required with probe or cancel; prevents stale calls from consuming a newer attempt.

session_id.description: Returned by the first call. Pass it back after their app has run a flow to see what it did.

suite.description: Configure the declared application receipt suite on this session.

name: validate_integration
